desk.headline: Revenue up 45% to $10.75bn, beat; EPS $8.83 missed as shipping and marketing costs cut margin; no guidance
results: Revenue rose 45% to $10.75bn (41% at constant currency), led by Brazil (+50%) and Mexico (+47%); Argentina grew 26%.
Income from operations fell 6% to $676m and the margin slipped to 6.3%, hit by more free shipping, new warehouse capacity before peak season and more affiliate marketing in Brazil.
Net income still rose 6% to $448m thanks to a lower tax rate and smaller currency losses.
Fintech users reached 93m (+29%) and the credit book grew 62% to almost $18bn, with early-stage bad loans steady at 7.0%.
Advertising revenue grew 58% in dollars; adjusted free cash flow was $285m after heavy credit growth.

guidance.summary: MercadoLibre gives no financial guidance. The shareholder letter says it is deliberately trading some margin today for growth and expects profitability to improve gradually as investments mature, without a timeline.

points: Management says it is choosing to invest part of today's margin to build buying and banking habits across Latin America.
Cost per shipment in Brazil fell 5% y/y in local currency; it expects scale and automation to lower shipping costs over time.
Mexico growth slowed on a tax change and weaker consumer spending, though market share still rose.
Credit cards are the largest fintech investment (almost $450m over 12 months); newer card batches lose money at first.
call.source: Shareholder letter in Exhibit 99.1; no reliable call coverage found

watch: Whether the operating margin stabilises or keeps falling below 6.3% through the holiday peak.
Credit quality as the card book keeps growing fast.
Mexico demand after the tax reform.
